Integration workspace for the frozen `hft-full-system-fpga` HFT baseline and frozen `RMIC` M5.4 risk-management core.

## Repository contract

This is the **only** repository where HFT/RMIC integration glue, adapters, futures accounting, policy logic, integration tops and cross-project verification are developed.

Pinned read-only upstreams:

- HFT: `Eric99720/hft-full-system-fpga` @ `50217fad1fd580f8c451ba893f9035f4be1dc21a`
- RMIC: `Eric99720/RMIC` @ `de6c300f4f18b18296f013287ab0eca70d3abb72`

Do not modify source inside `deps/`. A pin change is a separate migration decision and phase.

## Architecture

```text
market-data XGMII RX
  -> frozen HFT RX/CDC/order book/strategy
  -> frozen HFT 256-bit order_data
  -> HFT_RMIC field/account/product adapters
  -> HFT_RMIC fail-closed policy layer
  -> HFT_RMIC futures accounting/state
  -> frozen RMIC AMU/order-lifecycle primitive
  -> PASS: original HFT order payload
  -> frozen TMP R01 encoder / TCP / XGMII TX

TAIFEX R02/R32
  -> frozen HFT TMP decoder
  -> frozen HFT report-sequence owner (commit/dedup/gap handling)
  -> HFT_RMIC PositionEffect + before_qty side-band tap
  -> order_id -> futures order context
  -> futures FILL / RELEASE reconciliation
  -> context UPDATE / DELETE

TAIFEX R03 checksum-valid committed reject
  -> order_id -> futures order context
  -> release remaining reservation once
  -> context DELETE
```

RMIC does **not** replace the network layer, TMP session, decoder, order book, strategy, encoder, TCP/IP stack or PCS/PMA path.

## Current technical baseline

### Frozen HFT

The pinned HFT source is the frozen pre-hardware dual-XGMII baseline with market/trading ports, RX-HOT, CDC, order book/strategy, R01 fast path, ARP/TCP/TMP lifecycle/replay/flow-control and the accepted simulation-derived 83-cycle / 531.2 ns Gao-style nominal baseline. It is not board/live-exchange sign-off.

### Frozen RMIC

The pinned RMIC source is the M5.4 dual-flow baseline with 4096-entry collision-capable AMU, conflict-free CL2EX II=1, concurrent unrelated CL2EX/EX2CL, account/order hazards, hardware fill/cancel/reject reconciliation and U50 156.25 MHz post-route timing closure.

### Integration-owned additions

CI-validated integration behavior includes:

- exact account/product mapping and TMP-side conversion;
- fail-closed policy shell and extensible reject namespace;
- TAIFEX TMP quantity/Side/OrdType/TIF/PositionEffect/ExecType contract constants;
- futures accounting v1 with separate long/short and OPEN/CLOSE reservations;
- R02/R32 PositionEffect + `before_qty` side-band metadata tap;
- multi-account/multi-product futures state manager with fail-closed reset/recovery ownership;
- 96-bit futures order context over the frozen RMIC AMU contract;
- committed R02/R32 partial/final fill, cancel and reduce reconciliation;
- IOC-style fill-plus-auto-release handling using `before_qty`, `LastQty`, and `LeavesQty`;
- R03 exchange-reject remaining-reservation release with delete-once idempotency;
- stale/duplicate quantity mismatch protection even if a bad old report is presented again;
- dependency/interface drift and project-governance checks;
- I2 OOC composition compile-smoke;
- a Vivado-2022.1 Tcl compatibility guard for the local OOC flow.

The v1 margin model is host-configured `margin_per_contract × gross open exposure`; it is a research risk-budget model, **not** a TAIFEX SPAN claim.

## Verification entry points

Full local preflight:

```powershell
pwsh .\scripts\setup.ps1
pwsh .\scripts\preflight.ps1
```

Individual fast regressions:

```text
bash scripts/run_adapter_iverilog.sh
bash scripts/run_accounting_iverilog.sh
bash scripts/run_state_manager_iverilog.sh
bash scripts/run_order_context_iverilog.sh
bash scripts/run_execution_bridge_iverilog.sh
bash scripts/run_i2_ooc_compile_iverilog.sh
```

I2 real-AMU OOC/post-route gate:

```powershell
pwsh .\scripts\run_i2_ooc_impl.ps1
```

The Vivado runner verifies dependency pins, compiles the real pinned `deps/RMIC` XPM AMU, requires block RAM after synthesis, routes the I2 composition at 6.400 ns, rejects negative routed WNS, and packages reports/logs into `build\packages\HFT_RMIC_i2_ooc_impl_*.zip`.

The first local I2 invocation exposed only a Vivado 2022.1 Tcl API mismatch (`read_verilog -include_dirs` is unsupported). The current flow uses an ephemeral in-memory fileset with `set_property include_dirs` and is protected by CI so that unsupported syntax cannot silently return.

Vivado sign-off target unless superseded by a durable decision:

```text
Vivado 2022.1
xcu50-fsvh2104-2-e
156.25 MHz / 6.400 ns
```

## External network/PHY candidate

A user-supplied junior U50/network bundle has been audited but is **not** part of the frozen HFT baseline. It contains useful candidates — TCP-options-aware RX parsing, SYN retry, optional static-MAC lab mode, and a custom U50 10G PCS/GT backend with supplied board evidence — but its embedded HFT source snapshot has unpinned/version-drifted content outside the network overrides.

Therefore the current HFT pin is unchanged. Selective migration is deferred to a dedicated phase with exact source pinning, focused regressions, board reproduction and matched A/B measurements. See [`docs/research_notes/hft_network_candidate_audit.md`](docs/research_notes/hft_network_candidate_audit.md) and `D-20260917-09`.

## Evidence policy

Claims are separated into source/spec, functional simulation, synthesis/OOC, post-route and hardware/live-system evidence. Simulation latency is not board latency; routed timing is not physical packet latency; vectorless power is not measured board power. See [`docs/results_policy.md`](docs/results_policy.md).

No exchange-specific rule is called compliant until validated against the named authoritative TAIFEX version and the required integration evidence.

## Research direction

The frozen M5.4 RMIC is treated as architecturally complete for generic transactional risk/order lifecycle. TAIFEX futures completeness is an integration responsibility: OPEN/CLOSE and long/short accounting, margin policy, committed execution idempotency, readiness/recovery, rate/outstanding limits, end-to-end byte correctness, timing/resource A/B comparison and eventual hardware validation.
